If a virtual asset account suspected of involvement in fraud has been reported as a watch-listed virtual asset account, and there are still unwithdrawn virtual assets or funds remitted (transferred) by a victim in the account, the virtual asset service provider shall return the remaining virtual assets or funds in the watch-listed virtual asset account to the victim after receiving a written notification from the judicial police authority that provided the notification to the virtual asset service provider, and notify the customer holding the virtual asset account.
When a virtual asset service provider returns the remaining virtual assets in a watch-listed virtual asset account in accordance with the preceding paragraph, it may first sell the remaining virtual assets in the watch-listed virtual asset account through the virtual asset service provider, and then return the proceeds of such sale to the victim.

When a virtual asset service provider carries out the procedures described in the preceding article, it shall notify the victims through the remitting (transferring) virtual asset service provider, deposit business institution, or electronic payment institution to prepare the following documents. Thereafter, based on the chronological order of inward remittances (transfers), the virtual asset service provider shall identify, transaction by transaction, the portions that have not yet been withdrawn or transferred, and return the remaining virtual assets or funds held in the watch-listed account to victims, starting from the amount of the last transaction and working backward until the balance of virtual assets or funds in the account reaches zero:
1. Identity certification document.
2. A certificate or document of case acceptance (processing) issued by the judicial police authority.
3. An undertaking issued by the victim stating that he or she will bear all liability for any damages incurred by the virtual asset service provider due to untrue information provided by such victim.
When virtual asset service providers process the return of remaining virtual assets or funds in a watch-listed virtual asset account, other virtual asset service providers, deposit business institutions, and electronic payment institutions shall, within the necessary scope, cooperate to provide information required for the return operations, including remitting account information, remittance time, remitted amount, virtual asset accounts, and other information sufficient to confirm the order and amount of the return.
The fields, format, timing of provision, notification methods, and operating procedures for the information in the preceding paragraph shall be formulated by the Taiwan Virtual Asset Service Provider Association in consultation with the Bankers Association of the Republic of China and the Electronic Payment Association of R.O.C., and reported to the competent authority for record.

With respect to returning the remaining virtual assets or funds held in a watch-listed virtual asset account pursuant to the preceding two articles, if any of the following occurs, the virtual asset service provider may settle and close the account, record such remaining virtual assets or funds as a virtual asset payable or an account payable, and wait until a person legally having the right to claim such assets requests payment:
1. The remaining virtual assets or funds are below a certain amount, such that the cost of returning would make such return not worthwhile.
2. The institution is unable to contact the victim(s) within three months after receipt of the notification from the judicial police authority.
3. The victim is unwilling to report the case or to claim the virtual assets or funds.
After the virtual asset service provider settles and closes the account in accordance with the preceding paragraph, it shall not lift the effect of the watch-listing on the account holder until it has been notified to lift the watch-listing or the watch-listing period has expired.

If the virtual assets or funds in a virtual asset account have been seized, preserved, prohibited, or subjected to similar measures under another law, and the virtual asset service provider subsequently receives a notification from the judicial police authority described in Article 64 to return the remaining virtual assets or funds in the account, priority shall be given to the order for the seizure, preservation, prohibition, or similar measure with respect to such virtual assets or funds.

Deposit business institutions, electronic payment institutions, credit card business institutions, and virtual asset service providers shall designate a deputy general manager or officer of equivalent level to supervise the handling of balances or virtual assets held in watch-listed deposit accounts, watch-listed electronic payment accounts, watch-listed credit card settlement numbers, or watch-listed virtual asset accounts.

Cases identified by deposit business institutions, electronic payment institutions, credit card business institutions, or virtual asset service providers as being suspected of involving transaction disputes or otherwise complicated shall be handled through judicial procedures, and the rules regarding return of remaining funds or virtual assets in these Regulations shall not apply thereto.

To establish a fraud prevention platform, the establishing institution shall submit the following documents to the FSC to apply for approval:
1. Operational proposal specifying matters such as the purpose of establishing the fraud prevention platform, participating institutions, operational structure and workflow, risk and benefit assessment, and expected implementation schedule.
2. Explanation of the scope and necessity of customer information collected, processed, and used by participating institutions of the fraud prevention platform.
3. Agreements, templates, or explanations regarding rights and obligations among related parties of the fraud prevention platform.
4. Explanation of the information system and security control operations of the fraud prevention platform.
5. Other documents required by the FSC.
A fraud prevention platform that, prior to the amendment and promulgation of these Regulations on July 20, 2026, was established after being reported to the FSC shall be deemed to have obtained the FSC’s approval.

Participating institutions of the fraud prevention platform may use the services provided by the fraud prevention platform to perform the following operations:
1. Analysis or identification of abnormal deposit accounts, electronic payment accounts, credit cards, or virtual asset accounts suspected of involvement in fraud pursuant to these Regulations.
2. Operations related to inquiries, reporting, and account control measures pursuant to these Regulations.

To implement anti-fraud measures prescribed by the Act and these Regulations, the establishing institution and participating institutions of the fraud prevention platform may collect, process, and use customer information of participating institutions through the fraud prevention platform within the necessary scope.
These Regulations shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.
